AppTown tour

This is the AppTown a small team shares. Sam set it up. Tom looks after a cycling club's newsletter and a rocket game he made for fun. Priya runs the team's lunch orders and signs off on newsletter changes. Below, Tom asks for a new look for the newsletter, Priya decides whether it goes out, and it goes live. Then the club changes its mind, and the old site goes back. After that there's a quick look around the rest of AppTown. The chats are scripted for the tour, but the checks run on real code. Back to apptown.dev.

Unreleased preview · source local working tree · All versions

Projects

Three apps, all up and running.

Club Newsletter

Every app has its own page. This one shows what's live, where it runs, and a button to open it.

The site today

The club's newsletter as it is now. It works, but Tom thinks it's a bit dull.

Ask for a change

Tom asks for something louder. The agent changes its own copy of the site, checks the links still work, and tells him it's ready to try.

Try the preview

Before anyone signs off, Tom can try the new site in a preview. If it's approved, this is what club members will see.

The change

Tom's request and the agent's summary sit next to the checks, which all passed, and the preview. Now it's up to Priya.

Decide

Priya sees what she's agreeing to before she accepts. AppTown keeps a record of who said yes, and to what.

Accepted

Priya said yes. The change lands, and its release starts on its own.

Going live

The release builds the site, starts it and checks it before switching over. This site keeps no data, so there was nothing to back up.

Live

The new look, now what club members see.

Changed your mind?

Members found it a bit much. Deploying the earlier release again puts the old site back.

Back to before

The old site, back where it was.

Home

Where you start the day: your apps, recent work, and anything waiting on you.

Where the apps run

The machine the apps run on, how busy it is, and what's running there.

Conformance

Whether each app still follows the team's way of working, and what needs fixing. A few checks need services this example doesn't run, so they show as incomplete.

Ways of working

The team's shared rules for building apps: which tools to use, what to check, and how agents should work. Each app picks the ones that suit it.

Usage

What the agents have cost, and where the time goes, including time spent waiting for someone to approve.

People

Who has access, and what each person can do.

Docs

The docs come with AppTown, so they always match the version you're running.
